$comment: The PARAMETER layer of the worker's HTTP contract (#417), the sibling of
api-routes.json. That file answers 'which routes exist and what scope does each
demand'; this one answers 'what may a caller SEND to one', which is the half the
published clients actually drifted on: a filter the worker honors that no client
can express, or a name a client sends that the worker never reads, are both
invisible to a suite that mocks its own idea of the worker.
Keyed by the route `id` in api-routes.json, so the two files join and neither
repeats the other. A row here is a CLAIM, and inbound/route-params.test.ts is what
makes it true: every declared query parameter is proved LIVE against the real
handler over real SQLite (it must be strictly REFUSED when bogus, or demonstrably
CHANGE the answer), every name api.ts reads must be declared, and nothing declared
may be invented. An inert parameter is exactly the #413/#422 defect shape and fails
there, so this file cannot quietly describe a worker that does not exist.
query: query-string names the route reads. body: top-level JSON keys it reads;
'set.x' names a nested key. Absent means the route takes none.
Adding a parameter means adding it here in the SAME commit: the worker-side test
fails on any name api.ts reads that no row covers.

send.note: attachments are base64 over JSON (#70); forwardMessageId quotes a stored message, recipients stay caller-selected

send-alias.note: back-compat alias: the same handler, so deliberately the same list

reply.note: mode reply|replyAll derives the original recipients server-side (#363)

messages-list.note: lens needs a viewer and refuses direction (#403); under a session to= filters INSIDE the account boundary (#422); seenFor moves only the read-state projection key (#404)

search.note: mode fts|substr|semantic|hybrid; field pairs with substr; the view filters mirror messages-list exactly because they share one builder

recipients-recent.note: a bound identity wins; an unbound BYO token must name viewer= or to=, never an estate dump

folders.note: to= scopes the unread counts; a bound identity wins over it server-side

messages-seen.note: `for` writes a per-recipient override; under a session it must be the session identity (#410)

messages-move.note: mailbox archive|trash|junk, or null to restore the direction-default view

drafts.note: identity-owned: a static operator token gets E_IDENTITY_REQUIRED. PUT on an EXISTING draft requires its current updatedAt; an absent one is a conflict too, so an edit is read-modify-write

imap-drafts.note: the IMAP service seam: the door has no ambient identity, so it asserts the already-authenticated one on every call
